note: Divergence ratchets and depth floors for scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs. Lower a ratchet or raise a floor as the grammar improves; never move either the other way without saying why in the commit message. The measurement is only comparable against the flix-spec inputs recorded below -- a different pin or fixture revision is a different question, not a regression. Nothing checks those inputs: check flix-spec out at the recorded tag before measuring. Two ratchets, because there are two derived lanes: `divergences` gates structure modulo error recovery, and `recoveryDivergences` gates error-recovery shape on its own. Each lane also has a depth floor (`depthFloor`, `recoveryDepthFloor`, in percent), because unmapped nodes are skipped rather than compared: agreement once fell from 122 to 107 when the mapping set was completed, while depth rose 84% to 90%. A divergence count that falls together with depth is the number to distrust, and the floor is what fails the build on it.

oracle_conformance.comment: Re-measured against flix-spec 0.77.1, which pins Flix v0.77.0: a different question from the 0.75.8 baseline, not a regression against it. The suite grew 138 -> 147 fixtures and flix-spec's transparency now fires per occurrence, so canonical trees are about half their former size. Of the 101 divergences, 70 fall in fixtures that already existed (61 before) and 31 in the nine new ones -- most of those are syntax this grammar does not yet parse: `use pkg::...` package paths, effect type parameters, and the new match/ematch recovery shape. The four `elide` entries flix-spec now removes centrally (Expr.Expr, Pattern.Pattern, QName, UsesOrImports.UseOrImportList) were deleted with identical results; ModifierList and AnnotationList stay, because `elide-empty` keeps their one-child occurrences and removing them measured +48 divergences. `java_qualified_name` joined `ignored`, symmetric with `qualified_name`: a single-segment Java name is a bare Ident in the canonical tree (fixes try-catch). Then lowered 101 -> 85 by grammar work: `use pkg::...` package paths (the new `package` node, mapped to UsesOrImports.Package), effect type parameters, and generic effect operations parsed structurally as the reference parser does. nodesUnmapped rose 13 -> 17 because the package-path fixture reaches four more aliased_name nodes, which were already unmapped.

recovery_conformance.comment: Error-recovery shape alone, over the 28 fixtures whose raw reference tree contains a recovery marker (22 before). All 47 divergences in the previously measured fixtures are unchanged; the 9 new ones sit in new negative fixtures -- match/ematch with a missing body, operation type parameters, and the spaced package separator. The dominant disagreement is unchanged and diagnosed in flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md: both parsers reject `1_`, and they disagree about where the error is. Lowered 56 -> 55 by the same grammar work. Two divergences remain by design: for a spaced package `::` and a generic effect operation the reference wraps the offending part in an ErrorTree inside an otherwise complete node, and this grammar parses both without a marker -- it follows the parser's tree, not its diagnostic.

diagnostic_conformance.comment: The adapter emits `diagnostics: []` for every unit, so accept/reject is not compared. Emitting diagnostics from ERROR/MISSING/recovery-marker nodes is planned separately; it needs its own ratchet, because the lane gates the exit status as soon as any diagnostic is emitted.

source_invariants.comment: document-shape passes. The two vocabulary checks stand down because a projection map is in play, and token-accounting and token-positions stand down because this adapter emits no token text -- tree-sitter's named-node view has no Flix tokenization behind it. A structural profile, stated rather than implied.
